findings.where: "Where we're starting" section, the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok) with their "Best hostels ›" lines, at both widths
findings.fault: The cards look like links but do nothing. Each is a white raised card with a hover rule, and each has a "Best hostels" line in the link colour with a chevron. parts.txt marks all three as static, so clicking a card or its "Best hostels" line goes nowhere. The guides are the main place the brief wants this page to send people, and the page offers no working route to them.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps "Best hostels" for Canggu expecting the guide, gets nothing, and decides the site is broken or unfinished. The founder objects too: these SEO guide pages are the site's only content before launch, and this page leads nowhere into them.

findings.where: Nav "How we rank", and footer "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: These links go nowhere: each points back to this same page, and the page has no ranking section, privacy note or terms. "How we rank" is the one link that backs up the hero's "merit alone" claim. It sits in the nav with an underline, and clicking it just reloads the homepage.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who doubts "ranks on merit alone" and clicks to check the method. A careful visitor about to email their address who looks for a privacy policy and finds none. Both are left trusting a brand that publishes its methods less than before they clicked.

findings.where: The page heading order: the hero's "MantaHostels" title against the "Where we're starting" section heading
findings.fault: "Where we're starting" is set far larger than the hero title, about twice its size, and fills two lines at 1440 px. When you squint at the page, a section label beats the hero, the hero's message and the coral button. The page's loudest object is a heading that says almost nothing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the page. Their eye goes to "Where we're starting" instead of what Manta is and how to get launch news, so the hero's single action loses its pull.

findings.where: Hero, the message block: the eyebrow "The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.", the "MantaHostels" title, and the paragraph under it
findings.fault: The biggest type in the hero only repeats the brand name, which the nav already shows. The real offer (merit-only ranking, then booking direct with the hostel or through your usual site) is in the smallest type on the screen, a small paragraph that reads like a footnote. The only line at a readable size is "The better way…", a generic claim with no detail behind it. The brand's own rule is a loud claim with plain mechanics directly under it, and here the claim is the brand name and the mechanics are hard to see.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a five-second look who can't tell, from what stands out, why this beats the booking site they already use. The rules file's "loud claim, calm mechanics" rule is what this layout misses.

findings.where: Destination cards: their border, shadow and type
findings.fault: The cards break the brand in three ways at once. The border is a saturated purple that is in none of the palette's tokens; the card edge should be sand-border. A heavy soft shadow sits under each card at rest, which the rules ban ("Nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow"). The place names and island eyebrows are set in a typewriter monospace instead of Quicksand and Nunito Sans. The section looks like it came from another site.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand sheet sets the card edge, the faces and the no-resting-shadow rule. A visitor also sees the hero's beachy brand turn into a purple, typewriter-styled block, which reads as unfinished.

findings.where: Hero primary action, the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button, worst at phone width
findings.fault: The launch-news sign-up is a mailto link. The visitor has to open a mail app and write an email with no hint of what to say. On a phone without a mail account set up, the tap does nothing they can see. The label crams the whole address into the button and wraps to two lines on a phone, so it reads as a sentence, not an action.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone, often on a patchy connection, who wants launch news. Writing an email from scratch is more than a casual visitor will do, so the page collects fewer contacts than its job needs.

findings.where: Hero buttons: the coral pill against the square-cornered "Explore destinations" outline button under it
findings.fault: The two hero buttons have different corners: the coral one is a full pill and the outline one is a sharp rectangle. Neither matches the 8 px control radius the rules set for buttons. Stacked together, they look like they come from two different kits.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose rules give every button an 8 px radius. A careful visitor notices the mismatch at the one spot where the page asks them to act.

findings.where: Nav bar: "Destinations" plain, "How we rank" underlined
findings.fault: The two nav links look different for no reason: one is underlined and one isn't. The rules use a difference in the nav to mark the current page, so the underline suggests "How we rank" is either the current page or a different kind of link, and it is neither.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the nav, who gets a false cue about where they are, and the founder, whose nav rule gives a link a different look only for the current page.

findings.where: Desktop: the hero text column against the nav wordmark and the "Where we're starting" section
findings.fault: The hero text starts well to the right of the left edge that the nav wordmark, the section heading and the cards all share. The hero sits in a narrow column off to one side, with a wide empty space to its right. The page has no single line for the eye to follow.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning a trip, for whom the first screen looks loosely put together rather than "effortless", the first feeling the brand asks for.

findings.where: Footer line "Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali" against the Kuta Lombok card in "Where we're starting"
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, while the section above lists Lombok as a place Manta is starting. The page contradicts itself about where the service is live.
findings.who_objects: A traveller heading to Lombok, who can't tell whether Manta covers it yet. For a brand that says trust is the product, a contradiction on its own homepage weakens that.

findings.where: The whole page, on who is behind it and when it launches
findings.fault: A visitor is asked to send their email for launch news, but the page names no person behind Manta beyond the "luc@" address, says nothing about when it launches, and gives no reason to believe the merit-ranking claim apart from the dead "How we rank" link. The brief rightly forbids inventing social proof, and there is none to show, so the page has nothing else here to build trust.
findings.who_objects: A wary backpacker deciding whether to hand an unknown pre-launch site their email. With no named founder and no timeline, the request feels open-ended.
